problem: Symbolic planners need a grounded PDDL domain (objects, properties, executable actions), but in an unknown environment none of this is available. Prior neuro-symbolic RL work (SDRL, NSRL, DPDL) assumes a fixed pre-grounded domain and a perfect or fixed perception-to-symbol mapping.
motivation: A robot with only egocentric, partial, noisy sensing must discover objects and predicate values while acting, and compile abstract actions into low-level operations. Doing this online would let a single lifted PDDL model serve many goals, scenes and tasks with explainable behaviour, without task-specific RL training.
key_idea: An online loop that starts with no known objects, alternates exploring, detecting objects and predicting predicates from sensors, symbolic PDDL planning and compiling actions into low-level ops, incrementally growing the grounded domain.
insight: Symbolic planning over an incrementally discovered, noisy symbolic state can beat end-to-end RL on ObjectNav despite a weak detector (about 51% precision). The ablation with a ground-truth detector (C_GT) shows only modest drops (e.g. objNav success 0.78 vs 0.83), which indicates robustness. False positives matter little because the agent acts on the highest-confidence objects and many false positives are irrelevant to the goal. Note that the comparison is not fully fair: the agent uses GPS/compass pose, which the challenge does not provide.
method: Belief state: constants C for discovered objects, per-object features (position, bbox, visual features), state features (pose, last-action success, occupancy map initialised all-traversable), and predicate predictors; all start empty.
Explore: when the planner finds no plan, sample a random free target on the occupancy map, run a path planner on a discretised grid, and execute the low-level moves until the goal becomes reachable.
Action compilation: abstract actions are compiled into low-level operations; goCloseTo uses path planning to a point near the object, pickup/open use the believed object (x,y,z) position.

Object detection and anchoring: Faster-RCNN (COCO pretrained, fine-tuned on 69k AI2-THOR images, 118 classes) on RGB, position estimated from depth, and new detections matched to existing constants by 20 cm position distance.

Predicate prediction: an FFN for On (bbox + one-hot classes), a ResNet50 for Open, and a distance threshold for closeToAgent. State atoms are kept if their probability exceeds 1-eps, and inconsistencies are resolved in favour of the action model's effects.

Planning loop: propositional PDDL planner with existential first-order goals, executing one low-level op per iteration for up to MaxIter (200-500) steps, updating the occupancy map from depth and action success.

setting.backbone: Faster-RCNN detector + ResNet50/FFN predicate classifiers (trained separately) + classical PDDL planner and path planner
setting.training_data: Self-generated AI2-THOR data: 69,095 detector images, 36,344 On pairs, 48,476 Open examples; RoboTHOR detector fine-tuned on the 12 goal types, but no RoboTHOR-scene training data for the other components
setting.action_space: low-level: moveAhead 25 cm, rotate/look 30°, pickup/put/open/close at 3D coordinates
setting.privileged: none (but uses GPS+compass pose, which the RoboTHOR challenge does not provide); a C_GT variant uses simulator ground-truth detections

numbers.eval_set_note: 1800 validation episodes in 15 RoboTHOR val scenes, 500 steps
numbers.extra: uses GPS/compass pose (not in challenge); detector trained on AI2-THOR/12 types

numbers.eval_set_note: 2133 episodes from Wortsman et al. test goals, 200 steps, unseen test scenes
numbers.extra: 200 step budget; GT-detector variant: Success 0.83, DTS 0.19

numbers_note: The paper contains a second, unfinished RoboTHOR table (225 episodes; OGAMU 200-step Success 0.42, SPL 0.19, DTS 2.2) that conflicts with the main table (56.78/24.87). The main table was used, and the draft table is not included as an entry. The source names the method only via a macro (\arch), so 'OGAMU' is inferred from the algorithm description.
results: On RoboTHOR ObjNav validation, the method reaches 56.78% success and 24.87% SPL, beating the challenge winner DD-PPO_action_boost (36.61 / 17.49) and the DD-PPO baseline (35.11 / 17.37). On AI2-THOR it gets 0.78 success on ObjNav and Close, 0.75 on Open, and 0.5 on On, with a ground-truth detector giving only modest gains.
limitations: Uses GPS/compass pose, which the challenge does not provide, and evaluates on the validation split rather than the official test, so comparisons are not strictly fair.
Predictors and detector are pre-trained offline and fixed; the action compilation is hand-crafted; object matching uses a simple position threshold; exploration is random target sampling.
Low detector precision, position errors for large objects, collisions when carrying objects and stacking failures limit the harder tasks (On success 0.5).
